## Appearance

Isolde is an attractive woman with dark eyes, rosy cheeks, and black hair that falls in ringlets. Her cheerful look is a legacy from her father, and her complexion is marked with dimples when she smiles. As a child, she considered herself dumpling-like in figure compared to her peers.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c33 P13](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0013), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004)_

## Personality

Isolde is cheerful, practical, sweet, and comforting to her friends. She is a loyal companion who selflessly appreciates the talents and virtues of others. Though generally sensible and good-natured, she exhibits a humorous streak of practical skepticism and occasionally acts with mild defiance when irritated.

_Sources: [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026), [v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070), [v1 c21 P17](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0017), [v1 c37 P19](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0019), [v3 c12 P59](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0059)_

## History

Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill and formed a deep, lifelong friendship with Nell Harcourt during their school years at Brierley. As young girls, they spent their time exploring nature, naming local landmarks, playing in their secret playhouse, and founding a Story Club with schoolmates. Although their friendship faced a brief interruption due to a misunderstanding over homemade currant wine, they quickly reconciled after Nell helped treat a local child's croup. Isolde served as the treasurer of the Brierley Village Improvement Society alongside her peers. At age eighteen, she became engaged to Gideon Duckett and spent years preparing household items for her future home. After a grand wedding at Pear Hill, she married Gideon and moved to their new home. Later, she gave birth to her first child, a son.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c18 P25](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0025), [v1 c18 P43](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0043), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c29 P15](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0015), [v2 c29 P24](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0024), [v3 c12 P10](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0010), [v3 c28 P23](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0023), [v3 c39 P41](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0041), [v3 c39 P47](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0047)_
